video_title: Async Programming: Why Wait Is The Real Problem
core_insight: Async programming increases concurrency per thread by yielding on I/O instead of blocking a thread per wait, trading simplicity for massive I/O concurrency.

scenes.voice: Why does a thread-per-request server hit a wall? It’s not CPU, it’s waiting.
scenes.visual: Server handling requests, threads piling up while each waits on DB/HTTP icons.

scenes.voice: Each request blocks a thread while waiting for DB, HTTP, disk. Threads cost MBs of memory, context switches add up, OS caps you at thousands, not millions.
scenes.visual: Thread stack memory bars growing, context switch arrows, limit counter.

scenes.voice: Obvious fix? More threads. But you’re paying for idle waiters. The constraint is waiting time, not work time.
scenes.visual: Waiter per table standing idle while kitchen cooks, vs one waiter moving.

scenes.voice: Async is cooperative multitasking on one or a few threads. One event loop acts like a single waiter: start I/O, yield, handle next task, resume when kernel notifies.
scenes.visual: Single waiter taking orders, handing to kitchen, moving on.

scenes.voice: Mechanism is non-blocking I/O plus explicit yield. Start operation, await, loop runs other ready tasks, kernel completion resumes the task.
scenes.visual: Flow diagram of loop scheduling tasks and resuming on I/O complete.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    Loop[Event Loop] -->|schedule| T1[Task A: send request]
    T1 -->|await| Loop
    Loop -->|schedule| T2[Task B: process queue]
    T2 -->|await| Loop
    Kernel[Kernel I/O Complete] --> Loop
    Loop -->|resume| T1

scenes.voice: This helps when you’re I/O bound with high fan-out and low CPU per request. It hurts for CPU-bound work. Async does not parallelize.
scenes.visual: Split screen: network calls fan-out vs CPU crunch.
scenes.on_screen_text: I/O bound yes, CPU bound no

scenes.voice: Trade-off: max concurrency per core, minimal overhead, maximal complexity. One blocking call stalls everything. You must audit all dependencies.
scenes.visual: One blocking call freezing entire loop, warning icon.

scenes.voice: Mental model: async solves waiting, not work. Never block the event loop. Offload CPU and legacy blocking code.
scenes.visual: Event loop as single point, with offload arrows to thread pool.

mental_model: Think of the event loop as a single waiter who never stands idle. Tasks are orders that explicitly yield while the kitchen works. Concurrency comes from yielding on I/O, not from more threads.
final_takeaway: Async increases concurrency per thread by yielding on I/O. Never block the loop.
